clue.text: Missile from Woomera losing nose and tail in explosion

indicators.note: in places the trimmed name inside the word for the explosion

parts.note: an explosion is a bang

indicators.note: the place name drops its first and last letters, its nose and its tail

explanation.surface: A rocket fired at the Australian test range at Woomera blows up and loses its nose cone and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Woomera is a rocket range in South Australia, so the surface seems to be about a test going wrong. Its inner letters OOMER go inside BANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Aboriginal throwing stick is a hunting weapon hurled through the air, a classic thrown projectile.

clue.text: Slattern thus held in honour.

indicators.note: held in means the word for thus is placed inside the honour

parts.note: the BEM, British Empire Medal, is an honour
so means thus

explanation.surface: Even a slovenly woman is held in high esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: BEM is the British Empire Medal, a British honour. The answer is also a twig broom, but here it is a dialect word for a slovenly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for an untidy, sluttish woman, also meaning a broom of twigs.

clue.text: Hamlet senior's afternoon resting-place

parts.note: in Shakespeare the ghost of Hamlet's father says he was murdered while sleeping in his garden of fruit trees one afternoon

explanation.surface: Where the elder Hamlet took his afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet the Ghost tells how he was poisoned 'sleeping within my orchard, my custom always of the afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of fruit trees is where the old king lay down to sleep when he was poisoned.

clue.text: Swedes lie, embarrassed by a bloomer

indicators.note: embarrassed means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Some Swedes tell a lie and are embarrassed by a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a flowering plant, the alpine flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine plant with white woolly flowers, so something that flowers.

clue.text: Date when soldiers arose, overcoming people

indicators.note: overcoming means sitting on top of, so the earlier pieces come above the next one in this down entry

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: arose means went up, and in a down clue going up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: The date when the soldiers rose up and overcame the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arose' turns GIS round to SIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret appointment, especially between lovers, is a romantic meeting arranged in advance.

clue.text: Stone little woman turns up

indicators.note: turns up in a down entry means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Meg is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A stone appears as a small woman arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about four sisters, one of them Meg.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone or jewel is a cut gemstone.

clue.text: As an object of worship, count me out

parts.note: to tot up is to count or add

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the two letters of me are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declines to be counted among the worshippers of an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'leave me out', but it is the anagram signal turning ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem of a clan, such as a pole figure, is venerated as a sacred symbol.

clue.text: 100 mph — one hundred! It's so bracing

parts.note: doing a ton is driving at a hundred miles an hour
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Driving at a hundred miles an hour is described as exhilarating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a ton' is British slang for a speed of 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invigorating or restorative is refreshing, like a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Timothy, Peter and I seen in the band

parts.note: P is a common abbreviation for Peter, as in the letter P on a list
an is an archaic word for and or if

explanation.surface: Three friends, Timothy, Peter and the speaker, are spotted playing in a band.
explanation.walkthrough: AN is an old form of 'and'. The band is an orchestra, and these are its kettledrums.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are the percussion instruments found in an orchestra.

clue.text: Without equal, but can't set the Thames on fire

definitions.text: can't set the Thames on fire

explanation.surface: A man so unequalled that he still couldn't do anything remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who 'can't set the Thames on fire' is unremarkable, but read literally it is someone with no lucifers to light it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless or unrivalled for the first; lacking any lucifers to strike for the second.

clue.text: Go to court about 200 points win

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for suing wraps the number

parts.note: to go to court against someone is to sue
CC is 200 in Roman numerals
S and S are two compass points, south twice

explanation.surface: A litigant takes their case to court over a disputed 200-point victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory or triumphant outcome is a synonym for a favourable result.

clue.text: Keep quiet about article — it's free

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for silence goes round the article

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is told to say nothing about an item that is being given away.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'free' is a verb: to release a slave from bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate a slave formally from servitude, a Latin-derived legal term for emancipation.

clue.text: As Tom says, retiring, first out of two object

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the whole run is read backwards
the opening letter is dropped from the word two

parts.note: an object or goal is an aim

explanation.surface: Tom, retiring early, objects to being the first of two to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns WO plus AIM backwards. Tom is a tomcat here, not a man, so the definition is the noise he makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat's vocal cry is the sound a feline utters.

clue.text: Georgia private eye wanting Caution to break in?

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a tec is a detective, short for detective
lacking caution is being rash

explanation.surface: A detective from Georgia, throwing caution aside, is tempted to break into somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: to enter a party uninvited is a playful sort of breaking in.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a party uninvited is to force entry socially, intruding where one has no ticket.

clue.text: Parachutes were first into this town

indicators.note: into means the word for leading goes inside the phrase this town

parts.note: led means were first, as in led the race

explanation.surface: Parachutists were the first to drop into this town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parachutes' suggests soldiers dropping in, but it means the fluffy seeds that float on the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The downy tufts on a weed's seeds carry them through the air like tiny canopies.

clue.text: Help the unmarried girl

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried means that letter is removed

parts.note: a maid is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Help is offered to the single girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spinster, but 'unmarried' tells you to take M (married) out of MAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance or support given to someone is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Care needed moving into a tent

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Care is needed when moving into a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Heed or close concentration is synonymous with careful notice.

clue.text: Wise men of the country follow one with vision

indicators.note: follow means the other pieces come after the word for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity story
native means belonging to a country by birth

explanation.surface: Wise men from one land follow someone who has a vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' puts MAGI and NATIVE after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone creative and inventive has foresight and fancy, a mind full of ideas.

clue.text: Bill, Bob 'and I: in a sort-of act in the circus

parts.note: AC is short for account, which a bill is
bob is an old word meaning to cheat or filch, so to rob

indicators.note: in means the letter for I goes inside the rearranged act
a sort of act means the letters of act are put in another order

explanation.surface: Bill, Bob and the speaker put on a kind of act at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort-of' rearranges ACT into ATC, and 'in' puts I inside it to give ATIC. Bill and Bob look like two men's names, but they are an account and a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic feats on the trapeze or tightrope are what performers do at the big top.

clue.text: Distressed mariners in touch with Tees radio

definitions.text: Distressed mariners in touch with Tees radio

parts.words: Distressed mariners in touch with Tees radio
parts.note: sailors in trouble reach the coast station on the River Tees through the broadcasting device on board

explanation.surface: Sailors in distress make contact with the Teesside coast radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole description: the device by which a ship in trouble speaks to the shore. MARINERS is an anagram of most of the letters, but the three Ts are not clued, so it is best read as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio set that broadcasts signals is the apparatus that sends messages from ship to shore.

clue.text: Mrs Leonowens to be left by Miss Lee

parts.note: Anna Leonowens was the governess in Anna and the King of Siam

explanation.surface: Mrs Leonowens is about to be abandoned by Miss Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Leonowens was the governess of The King and I. Annabel Lee is the girl in Edgar Allan Poe's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The maiden of Poe's last poem is named in its title, the lost love by the sea.

clue.text: What's the matter with the Manxman's pet?

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the Manxman's pet loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is wrong with the pet belonging to a man from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is famous for tailless Manx cats, so the cat word loses its tail. 'matter' is not 'problem' but the yellow fluid of an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter is the yellowish fluid discharged from an infected wound or abscess.

clue.text: Left no-one up' here helping

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: no plus one, with one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is left alone up here with no one helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NO plus I round to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving or share of food is a measured amount on the plate.

clue.text: The cost of being right

parts.note: the British idiom says someone in fine health is as right as a sum of old pennies, so being right has a price

explanation.surface: A remark on the price of always being correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'right as ninepence' means perfectly well. Ninepence was nine old pence in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum of nine old pennies is the price named in the British idiom for being perfectly well.

clue.text: Geographical feature one shown in a map

indicators.note: shown in means the numeral is placed inside the word for a map

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One geographical feature is marked on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide flat expanse of land is a landform shown in atlases.

clue.text: She's 5

explanation.surface: A woman is described as being whatever answer 5 is.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to the answer to 5 down, GEM. The answer is a woman's name and also a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, and it is also a green or blue mineral prized as a precious stone.

clue.text: City with electrical connexions, we hear.

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: leads are electrical cables or wires

explanation.surface: A city with good electrical links, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a city in Yorkshire, northern England. 'connexions' is an old British spelling of 'connections'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large urban centre in West Yorkshire is a major northern English city.

clue.text: Fashionable 'meals provided nearer the shipping centre

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
board is meals supplied, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A trendy lodging that provides meals sits close to the hub of the shipping trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping centre' suggests a port, but it means the middle of a ship: the word describes a position closer to the ship's centre line.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vessel, the term means located toward the middle, away from the sides.

clue.text: Sink or swim

explanation.surface: Whether you sink or swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop or dip down for the first; a quick bathe in the sea for the second.

clue.text: Not in the team now fielding

parts.note: in cricket the fielding team is out while the batting team is in
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A player has been dropped from the team that is fielding now.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in' and the side fielding is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being external or beyond the walls is the opposite of being within.

clue.text: Stocking many London shops with it

indicators.note: this word says the answer sits inside the words it governs, as a run of their own consecutive letters
the words many London hold the answer inside them, like shops stocking goods

explanation.surface: Many London shops stock a particular item of hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'maNY LONdon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The synthetic fibre is used for women's hosiery, and the word is often used for a stocking made of it.

clue.text: Mince pies none initially contained fruit

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters are cut up and rearranged
initially means take only the opening letter of contained

explanation.surface: Mince pies, none of which contained any fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pies' looks like a single dish, but 'Mince' is the anagram signal working on PIES, NONE and C (the first letter of 'contained').
explanation.definitionFit: The woody seed-bearing structure of a conifer is the tree's fruit in botanical terms.
